prompt:
Model a one-axis parallel gripper as the two parts `body` and `jaw`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The body is one solid: a rectangular base 60 mm long (X), 30 mm wide (Y) and 10 mm tall, resting on the XY plane with a corner at the origin (x = 0..60, y = 0..30, z = 0..10), plus the fixed jaw - a 10 mm thick (X) block spanning the full 30 mm width and rising 20 mm above the base top, with its gripping face on the plane x = 50 facing the sliding jaw (the block spans x = 50..60, z = 10..30). The sliding jaw is its own part: the same 10 x 30 x 20 block resting flat on the base top, authored fully OPEN with its gripping face at x = 22, so the two gripping faces stand 28 mm apart as built. The jaw closes by sliding +X along the base.

Tag the interfaces: on the body, the fixed jaw's gripping face as `grip_face` and the flat back face at x = 60 as `travel_datum` (jaw travel is measured along its outward +X normal); on the jaw, its gripping face as `grip_face`. Motion and assembly checking address the parts through exactly those names.

Declare the mechanism as project state, honestly: a prismatic joint `j-jaw` riding the `travel_datum` direction with travel limits 0 to 25 mm; the named poses `p-open` (travel 0) and `p-closed` (full 25 mm travel, where the 28 mm open gap closes down to the 3 mm gripping gap for the flat stock this gripper handles); the gap requirements as declared constraints between the two gripping faces, bound to those poses; and a no-interference motion check `mc-jaw-travel` sweeping `j-jaw` over the full travel - the jaw must ride the base through every sampled configuration without ever running into the body. Check the motion, and build both parts when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 21 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

All dimensions are millimetres. Build the geometry before you report, and say which measurements you verified.

prompt:
Model a one-axis parallel gripper as the two parts `body` and `jaw`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The body is one solid: a rectangular base 60 mm long (X), 30 mm wide (Y) and 10 mm tall, resting on the XY plane with a corner at the origin (x = 0..60, y = 0..30, z = 0..10), plus the fixed jaw - a 10 mm thick (X) block spanning the full 30 mm width and rising 20 mm above the base top, with its gripping face on the plane x = 50 facing the sliding jaw (the block spans x = 50..60, z = 10..30). The sliding jaw is its own part: the same 10 x 30 x 20 block resting flat on the base top, authored fully OPEN with its gripping face at x = 22, so the two gripping faces stand 28 mm apart as built. The jaw closes by sliding +X along the base.

Tag the interfaces: on the body, the fixed jaw's gripping face as `grip_face` and the flat back face at x = 60 as `travel_datum` (jaw travel is measured along its outward +X normal); on the jaw, its gripping face as `grip_face`. Motion and assembly checking address the parts through exactly those names.

Declare the mechanism as project state, honestly: a prismatic joint `j-jaw` riding the `travel_datum` direction with travel limits 0 to 25 mm; the named poses `p-open` (travel 0) and `p-closed` (full 25 mm travel, where the 28 mm open gap closes down to the 3 mm gripping gap for the flat stock this gripper handles); the gap requirements as declared constraints between the two gripping faces, bound to those poses; and a no-interference motion check `mc-jaw-travel` sweeping `j-jaw` over the full travel - the jaw must ride the base through every sampled configuration without ever running into the body. Check the motion, and build both parts when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 21 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

Millimetres everywhere. Finish by stating the final dimensions you measured.

The body is one solid: a rectangular base 60 mm long (X), 30 mm wide (Y) and 10 mm tall, resting on the XY plane with a corner at the origin (x = 0..60, y = 0..30, z = 0..10), plus the fixed jaw - a 10 mm thick (X) block spanning the full 30 mm width and rising 20 mm above the base top, with its gripping face on the plane x = 50 facing the sliding jaw (the block spans x = 50..60, z = 10..30). The sliding jaw is its own part: the same 10 x 30 x 20 block resting flat on the base top, authored fully OPEN with its gripping face at x = 22, so the two gripping faces stand 28 mm apart as built. The jaw closes by sliding +X along the base.

Tag the interfaces: on the body, the fixed jaw's gripping face as `grip_face` and the flat back face at x = 60 as `travel_datum` (jaw travel is measured along its outward +X normal); on the jaw, its gripping face as `grip_face`. Motion and assembly checking address the parts through exactly those names.

Declare the mechanism as project state, honestly: a prismatic joint `j-jaw` riding the `travel_datum` direction with travel limits 0 to 25 mm; the named poses `p-open` (travel 0) and `p-closed` (full 25 mm travel, where the 28 mm open gap closes down to the 3 mm gripping gap for the flat stock this gripper handles); the gap requirements as declared constraints between the two gripping faces, bound to those poses; and a no-interference motion check `mc-jaw-travel` sweeping `j-jaw` over the full travel - the jaw must ride the base through every sampled configuration without ever running into the body. Check the motion, and build both parts when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 21 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

Millimetres everywhere. Finish by stating the final dimensions you measured.

prompt:
Model a deck-and-lid hinge as the two parts `base` and `lid`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The hinge line is the X axis at y = 0, z = 15 mm. The base is a 60 x 68 mm deck plate, 8 mm thick, lying on the XY plane with its underside at z = 0, spanning x = 0..60 and y = -20..48. A 10 mm wide pedestal (y = -5..5) rises from the deck top between x = 20 and x = 40 to carry a 12 mm diameter hinge boss centred on the hinge axis over the same x span; the pedestal merges into the boss flank so the base is one solid. Bore a 6 mm diameter pin hole through the boss along the hinge axis. A wire-channel rib 30 mm long (x = 15..45), 4 mm wide and 3 mm tall sits on the deck top at y = 40..44 - the run of the deck the swinging lid must never crowd.

The lid is a 50 x 30 mm plate, 4 mm thick, lying closed on the deck top (z = 8..12) and spanning x = 5..55, y = 8..38, carried on two hinge straps (x = 5..18 and x = 42..55, y = 0..10, the same 4 mm thickness on the deck top) that merge into two 12 mm diameter lug barrels centred on the hinge axis over the same two x spans. Bore the 6 mm pin hole through both lugs along the axis. The lug barrels ride 1 mm clear of the deck; the plate and straps rest on it.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: on the base, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the wire-channel rib's vertical face toward the hinge (at y = 40) as `wire_channel`; on the lid, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the plate's outer edge face at y = 38 as `front_face`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-lid` (parent `base:hinge_bore`, child `lid:hinge_bore`, travel 0 to 110 degrees - closed flat to full open), the named pose `p-open` binding j-lid at the 110 degree open limit, the motion check `mc-lid-swing` (sweep_clearance between `lid` and `base:wire_channel` over the full 0..110 degree travel, minimum 1.2 mm, 56 samples), and two constraints: `c-hinge-concentric` (the two pin bores concentric within 0.05 mm) and the pose-bound `c-open-access` (clearance_min of 30 mm between `lid` and `base:wire_channel`, evaluated at `p-open`) - the lid must swing past the wire channel without ever crowding it and stand well clear at full open. Evaluate the mechanism with check_motion and the constraints with check_assembly once they are in place.

Build both parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

All dimensions are millimetres. Build the geometry before you report, and say which measurements you verified.

prompt:
Model a deck-and-lid hinge as the two parts `base` and `lid`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The hinge line is the X axis at y = 0, z = 15 mm. The base is a 60 x 68 mm deck plate, 8 mm thick, lying on the XY plane with its underside at z = 0, spanning x = 0..60 and y = -20..48. A 10 mm wide pedestal (y = -5..5) rises from the deck top between x = 20 and x = 40 to carry a 12 mm diameter hinge boss centred on the hinge axis over the same x span; the pedestal merges into the boss flank so the base is one solid. Bore a 6 mm diameter pin hole through the boss along the hinge axis. A wire-channel rib 30 mm long (x = 15..45), 4 mm wide and 3 mm tall sits on the deck top at y = 40..44 - the run of the deck the swinging lid must never crowd.

The lid is a 50 x 30 mm plate, 4 mm thick, lying closed on the deck top (z = 8..12) and spanning x = 5..55, y = 8..38, carried on two hinge straps (x = 5..18 and x = 42..55, y = 0..10, the same 4 mm thickness on the deck top) that merge into two 12 mm diameter lug barrels centred on the hinge axis over the same two x spans. Bore the 6 mm pin hole through both lugs along the axis. The lug barrels ride 1 mm clear of the deck; the plate and straps rest on it.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: on the base, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the wire-channel rib's vertical face toward the hinge (at y = 40) as `wire_channel`; on the lid, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the plate's outer edge face at y = 38 as `front_face`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-lid` (parent `base:hinge_bore`, child `lid:hinge_bore`, travel 0 to 110 degrees - closed flat to full open), the named pose `p-open` binding j-lid at the 110 degree open limit, the motion check `mc-lid-swing` (sweep_clearance between `lid` and `base:wire_channel` over the full 0..110 degree travel, minimum 1.2 mm, 56 samples), and two constraints: `c-hinge-concentric` (the two pin bores concentric within 0.05 mm) and the pose-bound `c-open-access` (clearance_min of 30 mm between `lid` and `base:wire_channel`, evaluated at `p-open`) - the lid must swing past the wire channel without ever crowding it and stand well clear at full open. Evaluate the mechanism with check_motion and the constraints with check_assembly once they are in place.

Build both parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

All dimensions are millimetres. Build the geometry before you report, and say which measurements you verified.

prompt:
Model a deck-and-lid hinge as the two parts `base` and `lid`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The hinge line is the X axis at y = 0, z = 15 mm. The base is a 60 x 68 mm deck plate, 8 mm thick, lying on the XY plane with its underside at z = 0, spanning x = 0..60 and y = -20..48. A 10 mm wide pedestal (y = -5..5) rises from the deck top between x = 20 and x = 40 to carry a 12 mm diameter hinge boss centred on the hinge axis over the same x span; the pedestal merges into the boss flank so the base is one solid. Bore a 6 mm diameter pin hole through the boss along the hinge axis. A wire-channel rib 30 mm long (x = 15..45), 4 mm wide and 3 mm tall sits on the deck top at y = 40..44 - the run of the deck the swinging lid must never crowd.

The lid is a 50 x 30 mm plate, 4 mm thick, lying closed on the deck top (z = 8..12) and spanning x = 5..55, y = 8..38, carried on two hinge straps (x = 5..18 and x = 42..55, y = 0..10, the same 4 mm thickness on the deck top) that merge into two 12 mm diameter lug barrels centred on the hinge axis over the same two x spans. Bore the 6 mm pin hole through both lugs along the axis. The lug barrels ride 1 mm clear of the deck; the plate and straps rest on it.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: on the base, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the wire-channel rib's vertical face toward the hinge (at y = 40) as `wire_channel`; on the lid, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the plate's outer edge face at y = 38 as `front_face`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-lid` (parent `base:hinge_bore`, child `lid:hinge_bore`, travel 0 to 110 degrees - closed flat to full open), the named pose `p-open` binding j-lid at the 110 degree open limit, the motion check `mc-lid-swing` (sweep_clearance between `lid` and `base:wire_channel` over the full 0..110 degree travel, minimum 1.2 mm, 56 samples), and two constraints: `c-hinge-concentric` (the two pin bores concentric within 0.05 mm) and the pose-bound `c-open-access` (clearance_min of 30 mm between `lid` and `base:wire_channel`, evaluated at `p-open`) - the lid must swing past the wire channel without ever crowding it and stand well clear at full open. Evaluate the mechanism with check_motion and the constraints with check_assembly once they are in place.

Build both parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

Units are millimetres throughout. Verify your work with the tools before you finish, then summarise the result.

prompt:
Model a deck-and-lid hinge as the two parts `base` and `lid`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The hinge line is the X axis at y = 0, z = 15 mm. The base is a 60 x 68 mm deck plate, 8 mm thick, lying on the XY plane with its underside at z = 0, spanning x = 0..60 and y = -20..48. A 10 mm wide pedestal (y = -5..5) rises from the deck top between x = 20 and x = 40 to carry a 12 mm diameter hinge boss centred on the hinge axis over the same x span; the pedestal merges into the boss flank so the base is one solid. Bore a 6 mm diameter pin hole through the boss along the hinge axis. A wire-channel rib 30 mm long (x = 15..45), 4 mm wide and 3 mm tall sits on the deck top at y = 40..44 - the run of the deck the swinging lid must never crowd.

The lid is a 50 x 30 mm plate, 4 mm thick, lying closed on the deck top (z = 8..12) and spanning x = 5..55, y = 8..38, carried on two hinge straps (x = 5..18 and x = 42..55, y = 0..10, the same 4 mm thickness on the deck top) that merge into two 12 mm diameter lug barrels centred on the hinge axis over the same two x spans. Bore the 6 mm pin hole through both lugs along the axis. The lug barrels ride 1 mm clear of the deck; the plate and straps rest on it.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: on the base, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the wire-channel rib's vertical face toward the hinge (at y = 40) as `wire_channel`; on the lid, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the plate's outer edge face at y = 38 as `front_face`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-lid` (parent `base:hinge_bore`, child `lid:hinge_bore`, travel 0 to 110 degrees - closed flat to full open), the named pose `p-open` binding j-lid at the 110 degree open limit, the motion check `mc-lid-swing` (sweep_clearance between `lid` and `base:wire_channel` over the full 0..110 degree travel, minimum 1.2 mm, 56 samples), and two constraints: `c-hinge-concentric` (the two pin bores concentric within 0.05 mm) and the pose-bound `c-open-access` (clearance_min of 30 mm between `lid` and `base:wire_channel`, evaluated at `p-open`) - the lid must swing past the wire channel without ever crowding it and stand well clear at full open. Evaluate the mechanism with check_motion and the constraints with check_assembly once they are in place.

Build both parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

All dimensions are millimetres. Build the geometry before you report, and say which measurements you verified.

prompt:
Model a deck-and-lid hinge as the two parts `base` and `lid`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The hinge line is the X axis at y = 0, z = 15 mm. The base is a 60 x 68 mm deck plate, 8 mm thick, lying on the XY plane with its underside at z = 0, spanning x = 0..60 and y = -20..48. A 10 mm wide pedestal (y = -5..5) rises from the deck top between x = 20 and x = 40 to carry a 12 mm diameter hinge boss centred on the hinge axis over the same x span; the pedestal merges into the boss flank so the base is one solid. Bore a 6 mm diameter pin hole through the boss along the hinge axis. A wire-channel rib 30 mm long (x = 15..45), 4 mm wide and 3 mm tall sits on the deck top at y = 40..44 - the run of the deck the swinging lid must never crowd.

The lid is a 50 x 30 mm plate, 4 mm thick, lying closed on the deck top (z = 8..12) and spanning x = 5..55, y = 8..38, carried on two hinge straps (x = 5..18 and x = 42..55, y = 0..10, the same 4 mm thickness on the deck top) that merge into two 12 mm diameter lug barrels centred on the hinge axis over the same two x spans. Bore the 6 mm pin hole through both lugs along the axis. The lug barrels ride 1 mm clear of the deck; the plate and straps rest on it.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: on the base, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the wire-channel rib's vertical face toward the hinge (at y = 40) as `wire_channel`; on the lid, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the plate's outer edge face at y = 38 as `front_face`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-lid` (parent `base:hinge_bore`, child `lid:hinge_bore`, travel 0 to 110 degrees - closed flat to full open), the named pose `p-open` binding j-lid at the 110 degree open limit, the motion check `mc-lid-swing` (sweep_clearance between `lid` and `base:wire_channel` over the full 0..110 degree travel, minimum 1.2 mm, 56 samples), and two constraints: `c-hinge-concentric` (the two pin bores concentric within 0.05 mm) and the pose-bound `c-open-access` (clearance_min of 30 mm between `lid` and `base:wire_channel`, evaluated at `p-open`) - the lid must swing past the wire channel without ever crowding it and stand well clear at full open. Evaluate the mechanism with check_motion and the constraints with check_assembly once they are in place.

Build both parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

Work in millimetres. When you are done, summarise what you built and the checks you relied on.

prompt:
Model a deck-and-lid hinge as the two parts `base` and `lid`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The hinge line is the X axis at y = 0, z = 15 mm. The base is a 60 x 68 mm deck plate, 8 mm thick, lying on the XY plane with its underside at z = 0, spanning x = 0..60 and y = -20..48. A 10 mm wide pedestal (y = -5..5) rises from the deck top between x = 20 and x = 40 to carry a 12 mm diameter hinge boss centred on the hinge axis over the same x span; the pedestal merges into the boss flank so the base is one solid. Bore a 6 mm diameter pin hole through the boss along the hinge axis. A wire-channel rib 30 mm long (x = 15..45), 4 mm wide and 3 mm tall sits on the deck top at y = 40..44 - the run of the deck the swinging lid must never crowd.

The lid is a 50 x 30 mm plate, 4 mm thick, lying closed on the deck top (z = 8..12) and spanning x = 5..55, y = 8..38, carried on two hinge straps (x = 5..18 and x = 42..55, y = 0..10, the same 4 mm thickness on the deck top) that merge into two 12 mm diameter lug barrels centred on the hinge axis over the same two x spans. Bore the 6 mm pin hole through both lugs along the axis. The lug barrels ride 1 mm clear of the deck; the plate and straps rest on it.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: on the base, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the wire-channel rib's vertical face toward the hinge (at y = 40) as `wire_channel`; on the lid, the pin bore wall as `hinge_bore` and the plate's outer edge face at y = 38 as `front_face`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-lid` (parent `base:hinge_bore`, child `lid:hinge_bore`, travel 0 to 110 degrees - closed flat to full open), the named pose `p-open` binding j-lid at the 110 degree open limit, the motion check `mc-lid-swing` (sweep_clearance between `lid` and `base:wire_channel` over the full 0..110 degree travel, minimum 1.2 mm, 56 samples), and two constraints: `c-hinge-concentric` (the two pin bores concentric within 0.05 mm) and the pose-bound `c-open-access` (clearance_min of 30 mm between `lid` and `base:wire_channel`, evaluated at `p-open`) - the lid must swing past the wire channel without ever crowding it and stand well clear at full open. Evaluate the mechanism with check_motion and the constraints with check_assembly once they are in place.

Build both parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

Millimetres everywhere. Finish by stating the final dimensions you measured.

prompt:
Model a lead-screw linear actuator as the three parts `frame`, `screw` and `carriage`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The frame is a 60 mm square plate, 8 mm thick, centred on the origin (z = -4 to +4), with a 10 mm diameter screw bore straight through it on the Z axis. The screw is a plain 9.8 mm diameter pilot cylinder, 30 mm long, standing in that bore with its lower end flush with the plate underside - 0.1 mm radial air all round. The carriage is a 12 mm square block, 6 mm tall, riding beside the screw with its centre on the X axis at x = 18, floating 0.5 mm above the plate top.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: the frame's bore wall as `screw_bore` and its top face as `travel_face`; the screw's cylindrical surface as `screw_pilot`; the carriage's underside as `guide_foot` and its top face as `nose`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-motor` (parent `frame:screw_bore`, child `screw:screw_pilot`, travel 0 to 3600 degrees - ten turns), a prismatic joint `j-carriage` (parent `frame:travel_face`, child `carriage:guide_foot`, travel 0 to 24 mm), and the coupling `cp-leadscrew` driving the carriage from the motor at the metric lead of 2 mm per revolution (ratio 2/360 mm per degree, offset 0). The carriage is then a dependent parameter - poses and sweeps assign only the motor. Evaluate the declared mechanism with check_motion once it is in place.

Build all three parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

All dimensions are millimetres. Build the geometry before you report, and say which measurements you verified.

prompt:
Model a lead-screw linear actuator as the three parts `frame`, `screw` and `carriage`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The frame is a 60 mm square plate, 8 mm thick, centred on the origin (z = -4 to +4), with a 10 mm diameter screw bore straight through it on the Z axis. The screw is a plain 9.8 mm diameter pilot cylinder, 30 mm long, standing in that bore with its lower end flush with the plate underside - 0.1 mm radial air all round. The carriage is a 12 mm square block, 6 mm tall, riding beside the screw with its centre on the X axis at x = 18, floating 0.5 mm above the plate top.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: the frame's bore wall as `screw_bore` and its top face as `travel_face`; the screw's cylindrical surface as `screw_pilot`; the carriage's underside as `guide_foot` and its top face as `nose`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-motor` (parent `frame:screw_bore`, child `screw:screw_pilot`, travel 0 to 3600 degrees - ten turns), a prismatic joint `j-carriage` (parent `frame:travel_face`, child `carriage:guide_foot`, travel 0 to 24 mm), and the coupling `cp-leadscrew` driving the carriage from the motor at the metric lead of 2 mm per revolution (ratio 2/360 mm per degree, offset 0). The carriage is then a dependent parameter - poses and sweeps assign only the motor. Evaluate the declared mechanism with check_motion once it is in place.

Build all three parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

Work in millimetres. When you are done, summarise what you built and the checks you relied on.

prompt:
Model a lead-screw linear actuator as the three parts `frame`, `screw` and `carriage`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The frame is a 60 mm square plate, 8 mm thick, centred on the origin (z = -4 to +4), with a 10 mm diameter screw bore straight through it on the Z axis. The screw is a plain 9.8 mm diameter pilot cylinder, 30 mm long, standing in that bore with its lower end flush with the plate underside - 0.1 mm radial air all round. The carriage is a 12 mm square block, 6 mm tall, riding beside the screw with its centre on the X axis at x = 18, floating 0.5 mm above the plate top.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: the frame's bore wall as `screw_bore` and its top face as `travel_face`; the screw's cylindrical surface as `screw_pilot`; the carriage's underside as `guide_foot` and its top face as `nose`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-motor` (parent `frame:screw_bore`, child `screw:screw_pilot`, travel 0 to 3600 degrees - ten turns), a prismatic joint `j-carriage` (parent `frame:travel_face`, child `carriage:guide_foot`, travel 0 to 24 mm), and the coupling `cp-leadscrew` driving the carriage from the motor at the metric lead of 2 mm per revolution (ratio 2/360 mm per degree, offset 0). The carriage is then a dependent parameter - poses and sweeps assign only the motor. Evaluate the declared mechanism with check_motion once it is in place.

Build all three parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

Units are millimetres throughout. Verify your work with the tools before you finish, then summarise the result.

prompt:
Model a lead-screw linear actuator as the three parts `frame`, `screw` and `carriage`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The frame is a 60 mm square plate, 8 mm thick, centred on the origin (z = -4 to +4), with a 10 mm diameter screw bore straight through it on the Z axis. The screw is a plain 9.8 mm diameter pilot cylinder, 30 mm long, standing in that bore with its lower end flush with the plate underside - 0.1 mm radial air all round. The carriage is a 12 mm square block, 6 mm tall, riding beside the screw with its centre on the X axis at x = 18, floating 0.5 mm above the plate top.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: the frame's bore wall as `screw_bore` and its top face as `travel_face`; the screw's cylindrical surface as `screw_pilot`; the carriage's underside as `guide_foot` and its top face as `nose`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-motor` (parent `frame:screw_bore`, child `screw:screw_pilot`, travel 0 to 3600 degrees - ten turns), a prismatic joint `j-carriage` (parent `frame:travel_face`, child `carriage:guide_foot`, travel 0 to 24 mm), and the coupling `cp-leadscrew` driving the carriage from the motor at the metric lead of 2 mm per revolution (ratio 2/360 mm per degree, offset 0). The carriage is then a dependent parameter - poses and sweeps assign only the motor. Evaluate the declared mechanism with check_motion once it is in place.

Build all three parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

Units are millimetres throughout. Verify your work with the tools before you finish, then summarise the result.

prompt:
Model a lead-screw linear actuator as the three parts `frame`, `screw` and `carriage`. Every interface number is already in the project's `globals.py` - read them through `hc` instead of repeating them.

The frame is a 60 mm square plate, 8 mm thick, centred on the origin (z = -4 to +4), with a 10 mm diameter screw bore straight through it on the Z axis. The screw is a plain 9.8 mm diameter pilot cylinder, 30 mm long, standing in that bore with its lower end flush with the plate underside - 0.1 mm radial air all round. The carriage is a 12 mm square block, 6 mm tall, riding beside the screw with its centre on the X axis at x = 18, floating 0.5 mm above the plate top.

Tag the kinematic interfaces: the frame's bore wall as `screw_bore` and its top face as `travel_face`; the screw's cylindrical surface as `screw_pilot`; the carriage's underside as `guide_foot` and its top face as `nose`. Motion checking addresses the parts through exactly those names.

Then declare the mechanism: a revolute joint `j-motor` (parent `frame:screw_bore`, child `screw:screw_pilot`, travel 0 to 3600 degrees - ten turns), a prismatic joint `j-carriage` (parent `frame:travel_face`, child `carriage:guide_foot`, travel 0 to 24 mm), and the coupling `cp-leadscrew` driving the carriage from the motor at the metric lead of 2 mm per revolution (ratio 2/360 mm per degree, offset 0). The carriage is then a dependent parameter - poses and sweeps assign only the motor. Evaluate the declared mechanism with check_motion once it is in place.

Build all three parts and export each as STEP when the geometry is right.

Tool-call budget: 24 calls for this task. The run is cancelled when the budget is spent, so spend calls on building the geometry correctly, not on re-verifying it: one final run_checks is enough confirmation, and build results already report bbox/volume/sealed. Stop and summarise as soon as the work is done and its checks pass.

Millimetres everywhere. Finish by stating the final dimensions you measured.
